about: The archivist's catalogue: every kind of error found so far, why it happened, what fixed it and what guards it. Edited by a person; the archivist reads it on every run (archivist.py). No requirement text from Karimi's postings except the short examples a person chose.

entries.title: A degree the rules did not read as one
entries.cause: Degree names and the words in front of them the rules did not know (BS, BA/BS, B.E., HBO, WO, 'Relevant bachelor's or master's'), so the atom was read as a skill.
entries.example: BA/BS Degree in STEM -> 'BA/BS Degree in STEM' instead of Bachelor in STEM

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: A degree's field that is not a field
entries.cause: An alternative after the degree glued into its field: 'or relevant experience', a second degree, a language.
entries.example: Bachelor's degree or relevant experience -> 'Bachelor in or relevant experience'

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: 'is a plus' or 'preferred' left at the end of a requirement
entries.cause: Only words in front were taken as how much it is wanted; a closing 'is a plus' stayed in the requirement and made a new one.
entries.example: Experience with Go is a plus -> 'Go is a plus' instead of Go, optional

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: A requirement read as 'Desirable' alone
entries.cause: An atom opening on how much it is wanted ('Desirable', 'Advantageous', 'Preferred', 'Optional') is read as if that word were the requirement: the object after it is lost and the atom still counts.
entries.fix_hint: Take a leading marker off in normalise_req.strip_optional as the closing one is, and let atomise.nice_to_have see it, so the atom is optional and keeps its object.

entries.title: A requirement left in another language
entries.cause: The translator knew seven languages; Chinese, Japanese, Polish, Lithuanian, Hungarian and others were kept as written and nearly all came out 'nuovo'.
entries.example: Laisvas anglų kalbos mokėjimas -> kept as written

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: Translated, and still not English
entries.cause: A language sent to the wrong model (Polish through the Romance one, until 0.4.2), or a model that cannot read it.
entries.example: Wykształcenie wyższe w zakresie takim jak Informatyka -> unchanged after 'translation'

residual.measured_on: batch 1 of the new postings, rules 0.4.2, library re-run 2026-11-16

entries.title: The curator joined a category to a broader one
entries.cause: Taking a vendor or a generic word off in front of a category ('SAP EAM' -> 'EAM', 'IT platforms' -> 'IT'), and the judge passed it.

entries.title: The batch chose the language differently from the API
entries.cause: translate_must_have.py kept its own copy of which language and which model, so the dictionary missed what the library had learnt (0.9% of items).
entries.example: Polish items translated with the Romance model in the dictionary only

entries.title: A rule silently dead: a backspace where \b was meant
entries.cause: Patches written through a shell heredoc turned \b into a backspace character in two 0.4.1 patterns.
entries.example: Master's student never read as a student
